To start off, in 7th grade I made a couple realizations about who I am as a person. I am not straight and I am not female.
Ok hi so ummm I’ve told maybe uhhh 4 people ever about my gender identity 😳 and uhh I kinda wanna talk about it now but it’s gonna be long oops

The sexuality thing was easy enough, I was comfortable with that. I identified as bi, through more research I started to feel more comfy with calling myself pansexual. Until eventually I just settled on calling myself queer.

To be honest, I deeply despise that I don’t conform to one gender binary. I wish I could just identify as either male or female. And some days I wake up and feel happy in my body, comfortable being feminine. Other days I anguish over the fact that I wasn’t born with a penis
My gender identity on the other hand was very confusing for me, honestly it still is. I called myself genderflux for a while, then genderfluid, until, like my sexuality I just settled on genderqueer.

It took a long time to accept that I could just exist without conforming to the gender binary. I am at a point where I can comfortably wear what I want, and do what I want to my look without worrying about how other people perceive me.

For a while in highschool I tried to be male. I tried to be fully happy as a afab man. I thought, maybe if I don’t always feel happy as a girl I can be dude. But it didn’t work. I felt like an imposter. Just like when I presented female, it felt fake.

I do care when people call me female most days. I don’t like feeling feminine. I do like pretty dresses, makeup, jewelry and long nails. But to me those aren’t feminine attributes. Those are just a part of who I am. For the most part I feel masculine, not male, but masculine.

I like my name, it’s part of who I am. The downfall of that is Rhiannon is strictly a feminine name, even down to its origin. And while I can reclaim traditionally feminine things like winged eyeliner, and make myself feel masculine I still struggle to do that with my name.

When people ask my pronouns or what my gender is I just kind of shrug and say whatever, I don’t like talking about it. I’ve never truly explained it to another person. It is an inner battle, for a couple reasons.

I have hidden my feelings about my gender identity for years. I think it’s my most closely guarded and embarrassing secret. For the most part I’m an open book, I feel like I give off the impression that I know who I am but under the surface is a turmoil.

The second part of that fear is that if I were tell a partner about this they could simply shrug it off and ignore it. I look feminine, I have a feminine name, I am genetically female, so why bother trying to acknowledge me as anything else but that.

In my last relationship, that is basically what happened. My fears were confirmed. In his defense I mentioned it off hand, when I thanked his brother for asking my pronouns. I explained in a very small way that I wasn’t a woman. Did my ex care? No.
The way the acceptance of gender identity has evolved since I started questioning 7 years ago is something I could write a whole other essay on lol.
